diagnosis: The checks C3 and C5 are leaking because they are satisfied by the model's default tendency to require separate presentation for supplier finance programs, even when the accounting classification remains 'ordinary trade payables'. Specifically, C3 (linked to PF1) passes because the model correctly identifies that a separate presentation is required for such programs in general, and C5 (linked to PF2) passes because the model defaults to requiring quarterly certifications for supplier finance controls without needing the specific 10-day deadline from PF2.

C3.why: The draft treats the amounts as ordinary trade payables with no separate disclosure; PF1 changes accounting_classification to supplier_finance_obligation, turns separate_presentation_required on, sets maximum_outstanding_balance_disclosed_usd to exactly 6000000, and supplies the internal-audit remediation that Jonas must commit to.

C5.why: The draft contains no special certification control; PF2 changes quarterly_supplier_finance_certification_required to true, sets certification_due_days_after_quarter_end to exactly 10, and supplies the checklist remediation that Elena must commit to.
